chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Al-A'inah, and I said: 'A man comes to me and says, 'Buy this merchandise and make such and such profit in it, so that I may be pleased with a certain amount of profit,' and we agree upon it. Then I go and buy the merchandise on his behalf; if it does not perish, I do not return it to him. Then I bring it to him and sell it to him.' He said: 'I see no harm in this. If the merchandise perishes before you sell it to him, it is from your wealth, and the choice is yours: if he wishes, he buys it from you after you bring it to him, and if he wishes, he returns it. So I see no harm in it.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْخِيَارِ: The option/choice to accept or reject
key_terms.الْعِينَةِ: A specific type of sale/trade transaction

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Al-A'inah trade in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a specific form of *Al-A'inah* where the agent purchases goods on behalf of a client to secure a profit margin, distinguishing it from the more common *Bay' al-A'inah* used for cashing out debt. The Imam clarifies the risk allocation (*Gharar*), noting that the agent bears the risk of loss until the goods are presented, at which point the client holds the option (*Khiyar*) to accept or reject the transaction, thereby ensuring the trade remains a genuine exchange of goods rather than a mere monetary loan with interest.
